question: Five times the present age of P exceeds the present age of Q by 29 years. After 8 years, five times Q’s age will be 17 years less than seven times P’s age at that time. What is the present age (in years) of Q?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Test the given values to satisfy both conditions directly to save time.

Condition 1: 5P = Q + 29

Condition 2: 5(Q + 8) = 7(P + 8) − 17

Testing Q = 11: 5P = 11 + 29 = 40 ⇒ P = 8.

Testing Condition 2: 5(11 + 8) = 95 and 7(8 + 8) − 17 = 112 − 17 = 95 (Matches).

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Five times P's present age exceeds Q's present age by 29 years.

After 8 years, five times Q's age will be 17 years less than seven times P's age.

**Formula Used:**

If current age is x, age after n years = x + n.

 
 
 

 

 Present
 P's Age = P
 Q's Age = Q
 After 8 Years
 P's Age = P + 8
 Q's Age = Q + 8
 + 8 yrs

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let P's present age be P and Q's present age be Q.

⇒ From the first condition: 5P − Q = 29

⇒ Q = 5P − 29 ... (Equation 1)

⇒ From the second condition: 5(Q + 8) = 7(P + 8) − 17

⇒ 5Q + 40 = 7P + 56 − 17

⇒ 5Q + 40 = 7P + 39

⇒ 7P − 5Q = 1 ... (Equation 2)

⇒ Substituting Equation 1 into Equation 2:

⇒ 7P − 5(5P − 29) = 1

⇒ 7P − 25P + 145 = 1

⇒ −18P = −144

⇒ P = 8

⇒ Substituting P = 8 in Equation 1:

⇒ Q = 5(8) − 29

⇒ Q = 40 − 29 = 11

**∴ The correct answer is 11 years.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Constant Age Difference

The difference between the ages of two individuals always remains constant regardless of the time period (past, present, or future).

Present Age Reference

Always assume the present age as the base variable (e.g., x or y) to avoid confusion while framing equations for future (+ years) or past (− years) ages.

Linear Equations Application

Problems involving ages typically require translating the given conditions into a pair of linear equations in two variables, which can then be solved easily using substitution or elimination methods.
